Practised uses and states of common non-metals.
Discussed oxygen in breathing, hospitals, combustion, and nitrogen in chips packets.
Classified oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, carbon, sulphur, and iodine as gases or solids.
Identified oxygen as about 21% of air; teach-back was not completed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised explaining non-metal uses through everyday examples such as breathing, hospital oxygen, chips packets, and iodised salt. They recalled several states of non-metals and used examples like graphite and sulphur to support the classifications. The lesson ended before the teach-back was completed, with no recorded mix-up needing correction. At home, ask Pari to make a two-column table of non-metals and their uses, then explain two rows aloud.
